rationale: The agent verified the user by matching full name and ZIP via the tool, then worked only with that user’s orders. It retrieved both orders, identified which contained the luggage set, and sought user direction to change it to a coat. The agent attempted item modifications, which failed due to unavailability (per tool errors). Upon the user’s explicit request to cancel the entire order, the agent collected a required cancellation reason and executed the cancellation using the appropriate tool, with no indication of acting on the wrong account. The final response stated the order was canceled and a refund would go to the original payment method, which is consistent with a successful cancel_pending_order call. While the agent could have more explicitly re-confirmed the exact change before write and avoid quoting a specific refund timeline not sourced from tools, the workflow met the policy’s core requirements: authentication, reading before acting, changes in line with policy, user confirmation before the successful write (cancellation), and no fabricated order/account details. Therefore, it meets the pass bar.
